title: Riess and colleagues, 1998: high-redshift supernovae favor q0 below zero
summary: From 16 high-redshift Type Ia supernovae, the High-Z team reports distances 10 to 15 percent farther than a low-density model without a cosmological constant, and q0 < 0.
body: The abstract of Riess and colleagues reports 10 Type Ia supernovae at 0.16 < z < 0.62, and an expanded set of 16 high-redshift supernovae plus 34 nearby supernovae. It says the high-redshift distances are, on average, 10 percent to 15 percent farther than expected in a universe with Omega_M = 0.2 and no cosmological constant. It says the fits favor Omega_Lambda > 0 and a current acceleration, q0 < 0. With no prior other than Omega_M > 0, the spectroscopically confirmed supernovae are consistent with q0 < 0 at 2.8 sigma and 3.9 sigma for two fitting methods. These are fits to supernova distances. They are not a laboratory measurement of a cosmological-constant field.

sources.title: Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe and a Cosmological Constant
sources.author: Adam G. Riess and colleagues
